name: Marathon Petroleum
description: Marathon Petroleum buys crude oil, refines it into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and asphalt at 13 US refineries (about 3.0 million barrels a day of crude capacity, per the 10-K: 2,986 mbpcd) and sells the fuel wholesale, to branded independent dealers and through ARCO and Marathon branded stations. Its profit is the refining margin, the spread between product prices and crude cost, which swings with the cycle (segment adjusted EBITDA fell from $13.7B in 2023 to $6.1B in 2025). The steadier part is Midstream: through its master limited partnership MPLX it owns pipelines, terminals, gas gathering and processing, earning fees, largely from MPC itself under long-term agreements with minimum volume commitments, which produced more segment EBITDA than refining in 2025. It also runs renewable diesel plants.

employees.note: Approximately 18,500 full- and part-time employees, many providing services to MPLX for reimbursement; about 3,800 covered by collective bargaining agreements.

businessLines.name: Refining & Marketing
businessLines.how: Buys crude and other feedstocks, refines them at 13 refineries and sells gasoline, distillates and asphalt wholesale, to brand jobbers and direct dealers (ARCO stations) and for export; earns the crack spread, priced per barrel. 2025 adjusted EBITDA $5.63 per barrel; net refinery throughput 2,989 mbpd.

businessLines.name: Midstream
businessLines.how: Through MPLX, charges fees to move, store and process oil, refined products and natural gas liquids and gas; about half of segment revenue ($5,906M) is intersegment from MPC itself under long-term fee-based agreements with minimum volume commitments, the rest from third parties ($5,628M).

businessLines.name: Renewable Diesel
businessLines.how: Processes soybean oil, corn oil and fats into renewable diesel at Dickinson (wholly owned, 184 million gallons a year) and, with Neste in a 50/50 joint venture, at Martinez (730 million gallons a year); sold wholesale and under long-term contracts, with income from RINs, 45Z tax credits and California LCFS credits.

brands.name: Marathon and ARCO (trademarks "material")
brands.note: Jobber outlets: 7,882 brand jobber outlets in 40 states, DC and Mexico at 2025-12-31 (brands include Marathon, ARCO, Shell, Mobil, Tesoro); ARCO also sold through long-term direct dealer contracts.

brands.name: MPLX LP (sponsored master limited partnership, runs Midstream)
brands.note: Midstream segment revenue $11,534M; MPLX completed the $2.4B acquisition of Northwind Midstream (sour gas gathering) on 2025-08-29; MPLX had $1.12B left on unit buybacks at 2025-12-31. MPC ownership percentage not read.
